focus: fact retention under the v0.3.0 sentence rules; configurations: new_skill (v0.3.0), old_skill (v0.2.5), without_skill

evals.name: explain-code
evals.prompt: Explain src/token_bucket.py to a new engineer joining the team.
expectations: Fact retained: Rate limits are per API key
Fact retained: State lives in Redis so all replicas share it
Fact retained: Default capacity (burst) is 200 tokens
Fact retained: Default refill rate is 100 tokens per second
Fact retained: Uses Redis server time (TIME) so replicas share one clock
Fact retained: The whole check runs atomically as one Lua script
Fact retained: Tokens refill continuously based on elapsed time, capped at capacity
Fact retained: A new key starts with a full bucket
Fact retained: Each request costs 1 token by default; cost is configurable
Fact retained: Keys expire after twice the time to refill a full bucket
Fact retained: Redis keys are named rl:<api_key>
Fact retained: On a Redis error it fails open: allows the request and logs a warning
Fact retained: Fail-open reason: a Redis outage must not take down balance serving
Fact retained: Denied requests get retry_after = ceil(missing tokens / rate)
Fact retained: retry_after is at least 1 second

evals.name: explain-notes
evals.prompt: Explain the rate limiting decisions in NOTES.md to a new teammate.
expectations: Fact retained: Rate limiter state is in Redis because there are three replicas and the limit must be shared
Fact retained: Sticky sessions were rejected because partners don't send cookies
Fact retained: Rate-limited responses are 429 with Retry-After
Fact retained: 429 was chosen over 503 because the mobile client already backs off on 429
Fact retained: Silently queueing requests was rejected because it hides the problem from partners
Fact retained: The limit is keyed per API key, not per IP, because partners share egress IPs
Fact retained: Balances must never be older than 30 seconds (cache TTL is load-bearing)
Fact retained: Per-tenant quotas are not decided; default is one limit for all partners
Fact retained: Whether the mobile app gets its own higher limit is open
Fact retained: A partner hit 2k rps last month and made the mobile app slow
Fact retained: The user prefers a picked default over a config knob

evals.name: edit-target
evals.prompt: red-pen grid_section.md. The reader is product management.
expectations: Fact retained: Duration and grid are independent concepts
Fact retained: A 45-minute meeting on a 30-minute grid strands 15 minutes
Fact retained: Grid is set per meeting type by the firm
Fact retained: 30-minute grid types: kickoff, follow-up, plan review, review follow-up, office drop-in, hold
Fact retained: 15-minute grid types: intro call, quick check-in, workshop, other on-site session
Fact retained: Office drop-in is 15 minutes on a 30-minute grid, for half-hour arrival waves
Fact retained: On-site sessions use a 15-minute grid because meeting-room time is scarcest
Fact retained: Only three slots are shown by default
Fact retained: 45 should be a span on the 15-minute lattice, not a step size
Fact retained: Two 45-minute meetings tile a 90-minute block
Fact retained: Capability 1: fill a dedicated 90-minute gap
Fact retained: Capability 2: align to edges left by existing bookings
Fact retained: Slot score ranks by closeness to noon: Strong within 2 hours, Fair within 4, Weak beyond
Fact retained: Edge-based ranking was withdrawn because advisors rejected outside-in filling
Fact retained: Adjacent-slot checking code remains but nothing calls it
Fact retained: A dynamic edge-aware rule for fragmented days is parked, not a priority
Fact retained: 45-minute support is a placement change, not a ranking change
Fact retained: Adaptive grid shapes: grid follows the meeting, grid follows the gap
Fact retained: The booking UI passes the chosen duration as the grid
Fact retained: The duration/grid entanglement may be work in progress and needs a deliberate answer
